tags.name: Context-dependent
tags.description: A claim whose meaning depends on something introduced outside it: a pronoun or a definite reference ("the initiative", "the vulnerabilities", "recent actions") that no name inside the claim resolves, so a reader cannot tell what it points at.

rules.text: A pronoun with no antecedent inside the claim ("He said ...", "its predecessor", "they announced") makes the claim Context-dependent.

A definite reference that needs an outside antecedent to identify it ("the vulnerabilities", "the discussions", "the recording", "the settlement terms", "the legal dispute", "recent actions") makes the claim Context-dependent, even when other entities in the claim are named.

A descriptive definite that names a kind of thing but not which one ("the Bitcoin ETF", "the major-bank stablecoin consortium", "the open-access version", "the infrastructure", "the new model") makes the claim Context-dependent: the reader must already know which ETF, consortium, version or product is meant. Applies to countable things, not to abstract or mass nouns ("the regulatory clearance", "the market").
Test: could a reader who sees only this sentence say which specific thing each definite reference points at? If any answer is no, tag Context-dependent.
Do not use for indefinites, time expressions, generics, or definites the claim itself resolves.

example_claims: Open AI's initiative went well with the target group.
He said the new model outperforms its predecessor.
The company's revenue grew 40% after the launch.
Core Lightning developers are keeping the technical details of the vulnerabilities under embargo for two weeks.
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission did not comment specifically on the discussions.
The Bitcoin ETF successfully integrated Bitcoin into traditional brokerage accounts.

tags.name: Debate
tags.description: A broad, contestable claim whose central assertion supports substantive positions for and against it, rather than being resolved through direct verification of one narrowly scoped fact. It may express a policy judgment, comparison, interpretation, causal thesis, normative position, or broad forecast. A claim can be Factual and Debate at once; Debate classifies scope, not truth or quality.

when_to_use.preamble: Judge the scope of the claim's main assertion, not whether it is true and not whether it is currently argued about somewhere.

rules.text: Tag the main assertion. Concrete anchors, examples or figures attached to a broad claim do not rescue it ("The US has historically used inflation to manage debt, such as after WWII" is still Debate).
Naming companies or products does not make a claim Simple; scope decides ("OpenAI and Anthropic are the main competitors in frontier AI" is Debate).

Comparative-superiority stances ("X is better than Y", "X is the main competitor to Y", "X would choke Y") are Debate. A factual comparison of named entities on a checkable attribute (regulatory status, features, dates) is Simple.

Unattributed economy-wide or market-wide forecasts with no specific market, instrument or figure ("a recession is likely next year", "crypto will replace banks") are Debate. A forecast about one specific market, asset or event ("the largest wave of commercial real estate debt maturities is expected in the fall") is Simple.
Advice and "an indicator to watch for" state no checkable fact, so they fall to Debate; flag them for rewrite.

when_to_use.note: Open convention question: unattributed forecasts about one specific market with a figure and date ("the stablecoin market is forecasted to reach a multi-trillion dollar size by 2030") read as Simple under rule 4; round-1 gold said Debate. Recommended: keep rule 4 and let the Hypothetical tag carry the forecast flag.

example_claims: The US has historically used inflation to manage debt, such as after WWII.
OpenAI and Anthropic are the main competitors in frontier AI.
Entitlement spending in the US is not economically sustainable.
Bitcoin is a better store of value than gold.
Rising diesel prices are an economic indicator to watch for in the fall.

tags.name: Editor verified
tags.description: A claim a human curator has read against its source and confirmed to be high-quality and correctly sourced. It is a positive human sign-off, not a defect flag, and marks that a person — not a model — has checked the claim.

when_to_use.preamble: Human action only; never assigned by the AI tagger.

rules.text: Set by a curator after they have read the claim and its source and judged it sound.
The tagging pipeline must leave this untouched — it is a human gate, not a model output.
Absence does not mean a claim is wrong, only that no human has signed off yet.
Recorded here for completeness of the taxonomy; verification is of the convention (human-only), not of a model behaviour.

tags.name: Factual
tags.geo_tag_id: Not a tag on Geo: the Is factual checkbox on the Claim type, set to true.
tags.description: A claim that reports a specific thing that has already happened or currently holds, involving a named actor or object and anchored to a date, quantity, place, or identifiable event, so that it can be checked against a record. Factual does not mean true; it means the claim asserts something already on the record.

when_to_use.preamble: Derived on 8 Sep 2026 from 21 Geo crypto claims Moh judged factual; see the round-3 response doc for the set. Plan/proposal boundary confirmed 10 Sep 2026.

rules.text: Fires on an identified party's act on a date: announced, canceled, published, ranked, moved, exploited, halted.

Fires on an attributed proposal, warning, or stated reason ("proposed a draft circular", "urged users to exit, warning that", "citing security threats"). The claim asserts that the party said it, not that the content is right.
Fires on a reported cause of an identified event ("stemmed from a flaw in cross-shard receipt verification", "due to a compromise of the multi-signature wallet").
Fires on a standing capability of an identified thing ("EIP-7805 enables users to get transactions included without centralized block builders").
Fires on a currently set deadline or expiry ("have until September 10, 2026"); the fact asserted is that the deadline exists now.

Fires on the content or existence of a named, current plan or proposal — including its stated future design or effect — even under an "if approved" clause ("Once fully approved, Revolut plans to offer checking accounts", "the proposed redesign splits each instance's controls into five categories", "the corporate split will not affect users' holdings"). Only a genuine forecast of an uncertain outcome is Opinion.

Does not fire on an unconditional forecast, an unrealized hypothetical scenario, a value judgment, a recommendation, or a generalization with no specific actor and event. Forecasts and possibilities are carried by Predictive or Hypothetical.
Whether a source is attached plays no part in this decision.

example_claims: AUSTRAC announced on September 7, 2026, that it canceled, suspended, or refused to renew 45 remittance and virtual asset provider registrations over the preceding year.
The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas proposed a draft circular to suspend new registrations for Operators of Payment Systems for 12 months.
The August 2026 exploit on the Harmony network stemmed from a flaw in its cross-shard receipt verification.
EIP-7805, known as FOCIL, enables users to get eligible transactions included on the Ethereum blockchain without relying on centralized block builders.
Ethereum client teams have until September 10, 2026 to submit their ranked preferences for the Hegotá upgrade proposals.

tags.name: Hypothetical
tags.description: A claim whose main assertion concerns what could, might, or would occur under an assumed, proposed, conditional, or otherwise unrealized scenario, without predicting that scenario as the actual future. Under this taxonomy, past counterfactuals are excluded by convention. Split from its sibling Predictive on 4 Sep.

when_to_use.preamble: Sibling of Predictive; a plain forecast of the actual future is Predictive, not Hypothetical. Decide from the markers in the claim's own main assertion.

rules.text: Fires on a conditional under a proposed, potential or assumed scenario ("under a potential U.S. model, voting would require KYC"; "under the proposed agreement, holders will retain no claim"). SCENARIO FRAMING WINS: Hypothetical even when the verb is "will".

Fires on an unrealized possibility or capability that produces something not yet realized: could, may, might, can be designed to, can be used to ("platforms could compete", "tokens can be designed to generate revenue", "structured finance can be used to create rated instruments").
Does NOT fire on a past counterfactual ("the race condition could have allowed unlimited approvals") — a past capability is analyzable now, tag Neither.
Does NOT fire on an unconditional, scenario-free forecast of the actual future — that is Predictive.

Does NOT fire on a bare present standing capability ("borrowers can use Bitcoin as collateral", "SHRINCS keeps Bitcoin usable") — tag Neither; the thin line is against "can be designed/used to" in rule 2, which produces something not yet realized.
Co-exists with the Nature tag: a claim can be Factual and Hypothetical at once.

when_to_use.note: Verified 4 Sep on 100 crypto claims: glm-5.3-flash 98/100, glm-5.3 96/100, zero Predictive/Hypothetical bleed.

example_claims: Under a potential U.S. model, tokenized stock voting would likely require a user to be KYC'd on Coinbase.com.
Under the proposed Master Framework Agreement, equity holders will retain no residual claim.
Incumbent platforms like Coinbase's Echo could compete with existing ICO launchpads.
Structured finance can be used to create investment-grade rated instruments from SEDA.

tags.name: Improperly sourced
tags.description: A claim whose attached source, when read, does not actually support the claim's assertion — the source is present but the specific figure, event, or statement the claim makes is absent from or not established by it. Distinct from Unsourced, where no source is attached at all.

when_to_use.preamble: Requires reading the source (source-reading tag), so it is coverage-limited, not a text-only judgment.

rules.text: Fires when the source is fetched and read and does not carry the claim's specific assertion ('the price points the claim cites are not in the article', 'the country coverage the claim states is not mentioned').
Does not fire when the source supports the claim's core assertion even if a minor secondary detail is unstated (treat that as supported).

No attached source is Unsourced. An attached source that cannot be read is Source inaccessible. Access failure alone never justifies Improperly sourced, Factually challenged, Unverified, or a contradiction verdict; never report unread content as a pass.
Applies to factual claims; an opinion has no supporting source in the ordinary sense.
Validated 10 Sep on a source-reading pass over the fresh sample: 71% of sourced claims were checkable; the tag fired correctly on every checkable mismatch.

tags.name: Multiple statements
tags.description: A claim that packs two or more assertions that would each stand as an independent claim and each be checked on its own, typically joined by "and"/"but", "respectively", or a participle or "with" phrase that introduces a new measured value, actor or event.

rules.text: Split on coordinated finite predicates or clauses ("has ATMs, accepts Bitcoin, and features art"; "A and B, respectively"; "operate in X but lack Y"; "has become diluted and varies between entities").

A participle, relative clause or "with" phrase is a second statement when it introduces a NEW value, actor or event ("with Luke Evans playing Frank-N-Furter", "causing $1.78M in bad debt for Moonwell", "describing it as the best AI computer", "with 60% to 80% expected to be local", "vacating the designation and the boycott order").

A figure paired with a second figure that benchmarks, ranks, compares or re-expresses it is Multiple: each number is checked against a different source. Covers "earnings of $2.22, beating estimates of $2.09", "up 29% from the prior period", "Dogecoin rose 23% while Bitcoin rose 22%", a record ("the most expensive August on record") and a rank ("the first such proposal", "the second-largest loss category").
A non-restrictive clause that asserts a separate observation, not support for the main clause, is a second statement ("which was observed in early August").

when_to_use.note: Open boundary (Moh): a comparative subordinate clause naming a new actor ("where NIST schemes would choke") is currently left Single; flip to Multiple if such counterfactual comparisons should split.

example_claims: Nvidia reported non-GAAP earnings of $2.22 per share, beating Wall Street estimates of $2.09.
The California Senate approved AB 2409 in a 40-0 vote, and the Assembly voted 78-0 to concur on August 26, 2026.
Cypherpunk disclosed holding 323,394 Zcash, about 1.92% of the circulating supply, purchased at an average price of $341.83.
In the month prior, Dogecoin's price increased 23% while Bitcoin's increased 22%.

tags.name: Opinion
tags.geo_tag_id: Not a tag on Geo: the Is factual checkbox on the Claim type, set to false.
tags.description: A claim that expresses a judgment, interpretation, recommendation, prediction, or assessment that cannot be established as a past or present fact at the time it is made. Evidence may support or weaken it, but cannot remove the judgment or the uncertainty involved.

when_to_use.preamble: Counterpart of Factual; exactly one of the two applies. Factual covers what is already on the record; Opinion covers everything that cannot be established as a past or present fact when the claim is made.

rules.text: Fires on a value, preference, recommendation, or norm, often signalled by should, ought, better, worth, deserves ("peace is better than war", "abortion should be legal").
Fires on a forecast or prediction of what will happen ("the market will grow to a multi-trillion size by 2030"). Co-exists with the Predictive tag on the modality axis.
Fires on a possibility, conditional, or unrealized scenario ("platforms could compete", "under a proposed model, voting would require KYC"). Co-exists with the Hypothetical tag.

Fires on an interpretation, motive attribution, or analytic characterization that cannot be settled as a present fact ("the Treasury's actions are an attempt to control long-end rates", "functions as a back bid").

Does NOT fire when the claim reports something already on the record: a past or present event, an existing state, an attributed statement, a reported cause, a standing capability, or a currently-set deadline. Those are Factual.
A missing source, or an unchecked Is factual box on Geo, never makes a claim an Opinion.

example_claims: Peace is better than war.
Abortion should be legal.
The stablecoin market will grow to a multi-trillion dollar size by 2030.
The U.S. Treasury's recent actions are an attempt to control interest rates on the long end of the curve.
Rising diesel prices are an economic indicator to watch for in the fall.

tags.name: Predictive
tags.description: A claim that asserts the actual future will unfold a certain way: an unconditional forecast or expectation about what will happen, not tied to a hypothesized scenario. Split from Hypothetical on 4 Sep; operationalizes Yaniv's rule that prediction claims do not belong in the graph as settled facts.

when_to_use.preamble: Sibling of Hypothetical; a forecast under a scenario is Hypothetical, not Predictive. Decide from the markers in the claim's own main assertion.

rules.text: Fires on an unconditional future/forecast marker: will, is expected to, is forecasted to, is projected to, is set to, is likely to ("the market is forecasted to grow to a multi-trillion size by 2030", "the largest wave of maturities is expected in the fall").

The forecast must be about the actual future, stated flatly, with no "under X" / "if X" / "proposed" / "potential" scenario wrapper. SCENARIO FRAMING hands the claim to Hypothetical even when it says "will".
Does NOT fire on an attributed forecast ("analysts expect a recession", "X said prices will rise") — that is an observable statement, tag Neither.
Does NOT fire on possibility or capability ("could", "may", "can be designed to") — that is Hypothetical.
Does NOT fire on a scheduled event or a statutory maximum ("is scheduled to be sentenced on December 8", "faces up to 20 years") — an arranged or legal present fact, tag Neither.
Co-exists with the Nature tag: a forecast is Factual and Predictive at once.

when_to_use.note: Verified 4 Sep on 100 crypto claims: glm-5.3-flash 98/100, glm-5.3 96/100, zero Predictive/Hypothetical bleed.

example_claims: The stablecoin market is forecasted to grow to a multi-trillion dollar size by 2030.
The largest wave of commercial real estate debt maturities in history is expected in the fall.
Bitcoin will reach $200,000 next year.
The upgrade is set to ship in the fourth quarter.

tags.name: Self-contained
tags.description: A claim that identifies every essential referent clearly enough to be understood without surrounding context. Proper names are not required when a generic, indefinite, or uniquely descriptive phrase already makes the intended referent clear; the test is identifiability, not the presence of a name.

when_to_use.preamble: This axis is about entity reference only: does every pronoun and every definite reference resolve to a name inside the claim?

rules.text: Indefinite phrases ("a security researcher", "an illegal scheme", "one proposed exemption", "a potential model") never make a claim Context-dependent.
A pronoun or definite reference resolved by a name elsewhere in the same claim ("Nvidia ... the company"; "an illegal scheme ... the organizers"; "Strategy ... it") keeps the claim Self-contained.

A definite phrase keeps the claim Self-contained only when the phrase itself pins down one specific thing, usually because it contains a proper name, a date, or a unique title ("the supply chain risk designation against Anthropic", "the liquidations on Morpho on August 25", "the Commodity Futures Trading Commission"). Ask: could two different things fit this phrase? If yes, it is not self-describing.
Time expressions ("currently", "now", "in the fall", "sixty years ago", "the fiscal second quarter", "last month") do not trigger Context-dependent. Time anchoring is a different axis.
Presuppositions and generics ("retaliatory tariffs", "the increased program", bare "users", bare "investors", passive "is forecasted") do not trigger Context-dependent.

when_to_use.note: Open convention question: an indefinite that presupposes one specific unnamed event ("Attackers exchanged stolen tokens for $2.87 million") reads as Self-contained under rule 1; round-1 gold said Context-dependent. Recommended: keep the strict reading.

example_claims: OpenAI released GPT-5 in August 2025.
The shift to domestic chips supports Beijing's ambitions to substitute American technology.
Nvidia reported record data-center revenue, and the company raised its full-year guidance.
A security researcher disclosed a race condition in the Ledger Ethereum app.
Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.

tags.name: Simple
tags.description: A claim that states something specific and checkable: who did or said what, when, with what figures, or how one specific mechanism, product or practice works, whether or not a named entity appears. There is little to argue about beyond whether it is accurate.

when_to_use.preamble: Simple is the default on Geo: no tag is minted; a claim is Simple when it does not carry the Debate tag.

rules.text: Hedges ("could", "would likely", "is expected to") are not decisive. Hedged but narrowly scoped and checkable ("would likely require KYC on Coinbase.com") is Simple.
A named thing's function, feature, action or outcome is Simple even with an evaluative adverb ("successfully integrated", "failed to") or a figurative verb ("acts as a back bid").
Attributed positions ("X stated that ...", "according to Y ...") are Simple: the checkable fact is that the statement was made, whatever its content.

A claim with a generic subject ("borrowers", "users", "investors", "traditional methods", "BitVM-style bridges") is still Simple when it describes one concrete mechanism, capability, practice or pattern that could be checked. An evaluative or legalistic modifier ("fraudulently", "improperly") does not change that. It is Debate only when the assertion is a broad position with no checkable mechanism.
A claim about one specific product, protocol, company, person, law, event or time period, with a specific outcome, is Simple even when the outcome sounds broad.

example_claims: OpenAI released GPT-5 in August 2025.
Under a potential U.S. model, tokenized stock voting would likely require a user to be KYC'd on Coinbase.com.
SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell stated that the Starbase Louisiana project could eventually hire closer to 10,000 workers.
Borrowers in the United States can use Bitcoin as collateral for a down payment without having to sell it.
Traditional methods of obtaining leverage on Bitcoin involve debt, which carries margin, liquidation and duration risks.

tags.name: Single core statement
tags.description: A claim that asserts exactly one thing; everything else in the sentence only identifies, qualifies, or explains that one assertion. "X because Y", "X after Y", a list of objects under one verb, and an identifying appositive are all still one statement.

when_to_use.preamble: The question is how many independently checkable assertions the claim packs, not how long the sentence is.

rules.text: Do not split on coordinated objects of one verb ("demand for dollars and Treasury debt"), identifying appositives ("Open USD, a 140-member network that includes Visa, Mastercard and BNY"), scope quantifiers ("affecting 1,685 users"), or subordinate cause/time clauses ("after an attacker drained the pool").

A participle or relative clause that only re-states or renames the same event, with no new value, actor or benchmark, is still one statement ("ending the monthly unlock schedule", "threatening to burst", "which carries margin, liquidation and duration risks").
A single figure with its own units, date or scope is one statement ("held 323,394 Zcash as of August 11").

example_claims: OpenAI released GPT-5 in August 2025.
Stablecoins increase demand for dollars and Treasury debt.
An attacker drained the Morpho pool after exploiting a misconfigured oracle.
Open USD is a 140-member stablecoin network that includes Visa, Mastercard and BNY.

tags.name: Source inaccessible
tags.description: One or more attached sources cannot be accessed for review, so their contents cannot be assessed. This records an access problem without judging the claim's truth, support, or contradiction.

rules.text: Use when an attached source cannot be read after reasonable access attempts, such as a blocked host, paywall, login requirement, dead link, or unreadable document.
Identify the inaccessible source and any accessible sources separately; one blocked source does not mean all sources are blocked.
If no source is attached, use Unsourced instead.
Inaccessibility alone does not justify Improperly sourced, Factually challenged, Unverified, or a contradiction verdict. A separate readable source may independently justify another tag.
Remove this access flag when the source becomes readable, then assess its support separately.

when_to_use.note: Editorial rule confirmed by the editor on 11 October 2026; not an accuracy benchmark.

tags.name: Unsourced
tags.geo_tag_id: Not a tag on Geo: derived from the Claim having no Sources relation attached.
tags.description: A claim that has no Source relation attached on Geo. It is a completeness flag on the claim's provenance, independent of whether the claim is Factual or Opinion and of whether the content is correct; it only records that nothing backs the claim yet.

when_to_use.preamble: Deterministic, not a language judgment: read the Claim's Sources relation on Geo, do not read the text.

rules.text: Fires when the Sources relation is empty.
Does not fire when at least one Source is attached, regardless of whether that source actually supports the claim (that is Improperly sourced).
Nature-agnostic: a claim can be Factual and Unsourced, or Opinion and Unsourced.
Verified 10 Sep on a fresh 100-claim crypto sample: 9/100 unsourced; 91 carried a Source with a resolvable Web URL.
